classification.difficultyReason: Despite the supplied radii strategy, the student must organise equal base angles into a general proof, then reframe the outside-centre case using angle differences and connect both opposite-angle sums to the quadrilateral total.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Construct a large circle with centre $O$.

answer.short: A circle with its centre labelled $O$.
answer.worked: Place the compass point at $O$. Choose a large radius and keep the compass opening fixed while drawing the circle.

spec.description: Example of the requested student construction.
spec.mathematics: Circle with labelled centre O; radius is arbitrary.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Mark any four points $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ going clockwise around the circle and join up the quadrilateral $ABCD$. Make sure the centre $O$ is inside $ABCD$.

answer.short: Any quadrilateral with vertices $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ clockwise on the circle and $O$ inside.
answer.worked: Mark four points around the circle so that their joined quadrilateral contains $O$. Label them $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ clockwise and join $AB$, $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$.

spec.description: One valid clockwise cyclic quadrilateral containing the centre.
spec.mathematics: All four vertices lie on one circle, in clockwise order; O is inside ABCD.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Prove that these opposite angles are supplementary. Do this by drawing the radii $OA$, $OB$, $OC$ and $OD$, and working with the angles in the four isosceles triangles they form.

answer.short:
$\angle DAB+\angle BCD=180^\circ$ and $\angle ABC+\angle CDA=180^\circ$.

Equal base angles in the four radius triangles split each opposite-angle sum into the same four angles.
answer.worked:
Draw $OA$, $OB$, $OC$ and $OD$. Each triangle has two equal radii, so its base angles are equal. Let the base angles of $\triangle OAB$, $\triangle OBC$, $\triangle OCD$ and $\triangle ODA$ be $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$, respectively. Then
$$\begin{align*}\angle DAB&=\theta+\alpha\\\angle ABC&=\alpha+\beta\\\angle BCD&=\beta+\gamma\\\angle CDA&=\gamma+\theta.\end{align*}$$
The quadrilateral angle sum gives
$$\begin{align*}2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\theta)&=360^\circ\\\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\theta&=180^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}\angle DAB+\angle BCD&=\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\theta\\\angle DAB+\angle BCD&=180^\circ\\\angle ABC+\angle CDA&=\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\theta\\\angle ABC+\angle CDA&=180^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: The inside-centre construction completed with four radii.
spec.mathematics: OAB, OBC, OCD and ODA are isosceles triangles because all radii are equal.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Repeat part b but this time choose points $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ so that point $O$ is outside the quadrilateral $ABCD$. Now repeat part c. The proof this time will be a little different, because you will need to take differences as well as sums of angles.

answer.short:
$\angle DAB+\angle BCD=180^\circ$ and $\angle ABC+\angle CDA=180^\circ$ still hold.

Subtract the base angle of the triangle spanning the empty arc when forming the quadrilateral angles at its endpoints.
answer.worked:
Construct a new circle and choose four clockwise points on an arc shorter than a semicircle, as shown. Join the quadrilateral and the four radii. For this labelling, let the base angles of $\triangle OAB$, $\triangle OBC$, $\triangle OCD$ and $\triangle ODA$ be $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$, respectively. Equal radii give equal base angles. Here $\triangle ODA$ spans the empty arc, and
$$\begin{align*}\angle DAB&=\alpha-\theta\\\angle ABC&=\alpha+\beta\\\angle BCD&=\beta+\gamma\\\angle CDA&=\gamma-\theta.\end{align*}$$
Using the quadrilateral angle sum,
$$\begin{align*}2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma-\theta)&=360^\circ\\\alpha+\beta+\gamma-\theta&=180^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Therefore,
$$\begin{align*}\angle DAB+\angle BCD&=\alpha+\beta+\gamma-\theta\\\angle DAB+\angle BCD&=180^\circ\\\angle ABC+\angle CDA&=\alpha+\beta+\gamma-\theta\\\angle ABC+\angle CDA&=180^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The same subtraction argument applies after cyclically relabelling any outside-centre configuration so that $DA$ spans its empty arc.

spec.description: One valid outside-centre construction, completed with radii.
spec.mathematics: Vertices A, B, C and D run clockwise along the upper minor arc. O is outside ABCD. Triangle ODA supplies the base angle subtracted at A and D.
